activities.caption: call the magnitude — the logarithmic squeeze
activities.name: wcmPhEstimate

config.prompt: Each whole pH step is a tenfold change. Water at pH 5 versus water at pH 7 — how many times more acidity does the pH 5 water carry?
config.why: Two whole steps, two tenfolds: 10 × 10 = 100 — the reason engineers guard pH so jealously.
config.context: Half a unit is a big chemical shift: pH 6.5 is already about three times more acidic than pH 7.

activities.caption: rebuild the carbonate chain, gas to alkalinity
activities.name: wcmCarbonOrder

config.prompt: From gas to guarded pH — put the carbonate chain in order:
items: Atmospheric CO₂ dissolves into the water
It equilibrates through bicarbonate to carbonate
Dissolved limestone (rock eaten by that same acid) contributes alkalinity
Most natural waters end up held between pH 6 and 9
config.why: A buffer is a chemical sponge that soaks up added acid or base, holding pH nearly steady while it has capacity left.

activities.anchor: packages this equilibrium arithmetic as a single number
activities.caption: corrosive water in a lead-line city — pick the move
activities.name: wcmCorrosionBranch

config.root: A plant serves a city with old lead service lines. Its water tests on the corrosive side of zero.

choices.label: Nudge the carbonate chemistry and dose orthophosphate to grow a protective mineral film
Switch to a cheaper river and skip conditioning — the old source treated fine for decades
Schedule full lead-line replacement and wait

control.text: Index and pipe agree: a protective mineral film lines the old lead, and the glasses stay clean.

flint.text: The river carried almost no lead — its untreated, more corrosive chemistry dissolved the decades-old mineral scale that had lined the service lines instead.

slow.text: The water attacks the pipes meanwhile; conditioning and replacement run on separate timelines.

config.why: Lead is usually a materials-and-chemistry failure, not a contaminated-source failure — the discipline that keeps lead out of glasses is corrosion control.

activities.caption: first the form, then the amount — file each species
activities.name: wcmSpeciationBuckets

config.prompt: Same element, different pH, different bite — file each species:
buckets: the weak, benign or vanished form

items.label: HOCl — hypochlorous acid, the potent killer
NH₃ — unionised ammonia to a fish

config.why: In water, ask first 'in what form?', then 'how much?' — toxicity, solubility and disinfecting power are all functions of pH.

activities.anchor: and the water must leave them
activities.caption: pair each decay speed with the problem it creates
activities.name: wcmHalfLifeMatch

config.prompt: The half-life is a sorting hat — pair each case:

pairs.right: the time for half of anything to decay
the first-order law: decay proportional to how much remains

config.why: Pollutant degradation, pathogen die-off, radioactive decay and BOD exertion all follow the first-order shape — speed is the resource tanks buy.

activities.anchor: biological treatment slows painfully in winter
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the cold snap
activities.name: wcmWinterPredict

config.q: At a wastewater plant the water drops from 15 °C to 5 °C in a cold snap. What happens to the ammonia-oxidising bacteria?
choices: They speed up — cold water holds more oxygen
Unaffected — temperature only tunes chemistry, not biology
config.why: Rates classically halve per 10 °C fall — and the nitrifiers, the most cold-sensitive of the workforce, essentially stop below about 10 °C.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the disinfection plan
activities.name: wcmBaffleSpot

config.prompt: An operator's disinfection plan contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Chick's law: under a fixed concentration, microorganisms die off exponentially.
Chick–Watson: the kill depends on the product of concentration and time — the CT value.
Doubling contact time can substitute for doubling concentration — same CT.
So the theoretical residence time of our unbaffled basin is what counts.
Regulators publish the CT needed per log of inactivation, per pathogen, pH and temperature.
config.correction: Effective contact time is the theoretical residence time times a baffling factor — roughly 0.3 unbaffled, approaching 0.7 for a well-baffled serpentine basin.
config.why: Some water short-circuits and leaves early; when a plant needs more kill, the response is geometry — add baffles, buy time.

activities.anchor: The indicator approach is a bet
activities.caption: true or false — what the lab actually tests
activities.name: wcmIndicatorJudge

statements.s: Utilities routinely test for each specific disease agent.
statements.why: Testing each pathogen directly is slow and expensive; they test coliforms and E. coli — faecal bacteria that travel with the pathogens but are cheap and quick to detect.

statements.s: A positive coliform sample signals faecal contamination and raises the odds that pathogens are present too.
statements.why: Coliforms colonise in far greater numbers — the signal rides on their abundance.

statements.s: A negative coliform test proves no viruses or protozoa are present.
statements.why: Viruses and protozoa survive differently from bacteria — which is why modern rules layer several signals plus CT credit and filtration performance instead of trusting one number.

statements.s: Turbidity is purely an aesthetic standard.
statements.why: Particles can shelter microbes from disinfectants — clear water is a safety requirement, not just an aesthetic one.
